title: M-108

data.h1: M-108 Titanium Dioxide for Plastics and Masterbatch Evaluation
hero_paragraphs: The current product profile identifies heat stability, opacity and whiteness, moisture and oil absorption, antioxidant reactivity, resin compatibility and dispersion as evaluation directions. Review the technical data below and confirm suitability through testing in your own polymer system, formulation, processing and end-use conditions.

data.positioning_title: Where M-108 Fits in Product Evaluation
positioning_paragraphs: M-108 is an alumina-treated rutile titanium dioxide pigment made by the sulfate process for plastics and masterbatch evaluation.

Use M-108 as a candidate when thermal stability, opacity, whiteness, dispersion and processing compatibility are relevant. Final selection should account for the polymer, carrier resin, additives and antioxidants, pigment loading, processing temperature, equipment, film or compound requirements and destination documents.
facts: Alumina inorganic treatment and organic treatment
Evaluation of heat stability, optical targets, absorption, reactivity, compatibility and dispersion
data.applications_title: Plastics and Masterbatch Directions to Evaluate

applications.title: Masterbatch and Compounds
applications.text: Evaluate M-108 at the intended pigment loading and carrier-resin system. Confirm dispersion, color, processing behavior, antioxidant interaction and downstream dilution performance.

applications.title: Polyolefin and PVC Film
applications.text: Review M-108 in the intended polyolefin or PVC film formulation and production line. Confirm dispersion, opacity, whiteness, film appearance, processing stability and melt-flow behavior.

applications.title: Plastics Requiring High Thermal Stability
applications.text: Include M-108 in testing where processing or end-use qualification requires the documented high-thermal-stability direction. Confirm the result at the actual temperature, residence time, formulation and equipment conditions.

data.evaluation_title: What to Evaluate in Your Plastics Formulation

evaluation.title: Optical and Dispersion Review
items: Opacity and whiteness targets in the complete formulation
Rapid and complete dispersion under the intended mixing conditions
Finished appearance in the selected polymer or film system
Consistency at the intended pigment loading and downstream process

evaluation.title: Thermal and Processing Qualification
items: Heat stability at the actual processing temperature and residence time
Moisture and oil absorption in the formulation context
Reactivity with the selected antioxidant package and compatibility with plastic resins
Masterbatch, compounding or film conditions, destination needs and sample-validation results

data.evaluation_note: These evaluation priorities identify what to check during buyer testing. They do not guarantee a fixed result in every polymer, process or end-use environment.
data.technical_note: These values reproduce the current M-108 TDS and do not constitute a product specification. Moisture is measured within 48 hours of production. Confirm suitability in your own formulation and processing conditions.
